node_notes.usart2_tx: USART2 transmits the application's console output through TX on PA2. firmware/configs/app_config.h assigns PA2, and firmware/platforms/stm32/console_stm32.c configures USART2 TX and implements the newlib _write transport.
node_notes.app: The application initializes board I/O and the console, then runs the LED and button bring-up loop. firmware/app/app.c uses the board_io interface and LOGI messages to implement this behavior.
node_notes.systick: The Cortex SysTick provides the millisecond interrupt used by the firmware timebase. Core/Src/main.c configures a 1 ms SysTick, and Core/Src/stm32f4xx_it.c forwards its handler to the STM32 board I/O adapter.
node_notes.button_pa0: The STM32F4DISCOVERY user button is an active-high input wired to PA0. The platform adapter reads it with LL_GPIO_IsInputPinSet, as configured by APP_BUTTON_GPIO_PORT and APP_BUTTON_GPIO_PIN in firmware/configs/app_config.h.
node_notes.board_io: This STM32 adapter configures and reads PA0, toggles the PD12 LED, maintains milliseconds, and waits with __WFI. These operations are implemented in firmware/platforms/stm32/board_io_stm32.c and its SysTick bridge is called from Core/Src/stm32f4xx_it.c.
node_notes.led_pd12: The onboard indicator LED is an active-high output wired to PD12. The STM32 adapter toggles it with LL_GPIO_TogglePin using APP_LED_GPIO_PORT and APP_LED_GPIO_PIN from firmware/configs/app_config.h.
node_notes.console: The console backend configures USART2 for transmit-only operation and routes printf output through _write. firmware/platforms/stm32/console_stm32.c assigns the configured PA2 pin to alternate function 7 and uses the 115200 baud setting.

node_notes.toggle_led: When the LED interval has elapsed, the application toggles the indicator and records the current time. firmware/app/app.c:29-30 calls board_io_led_toggle and updates last_led_toggle_ms.
node_notes.led_due: This condition checks whether the configured LED period has elapsed since its previous toggle. firmware/app/app.c:27 compares elapsed time with APP_LED_PERIOD_MS, set to 200 ms in firmware/configs/app_config.h.
node_notes.sample: Each foreground iteration reads the millisecond counter and logical button state through board_io. The reads are in firmware/app/app.c:24-25, with the STM32 implementation in firmware/platforms/stm32/board_io_stm32.c.
node_notes.debounce_ready: When the sample remains unchanged, this condition checks for a difference from the stable state and expiration of the debounce interval. The compound test is in firmware/app/app.c:38-40 and uses APP_BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_MS from firmware/configs/app_config.h.
node_notes.wait_irq: The loop waits for an interrupt to reduce foreground polling, then resumes sampling after wake. firmware/app/app.c:47 calls board_io_wait_for_interrupt, implemented with __WFI in firmware/platforms/stm32/board_io_stm32.c.
node_notes.accept_button: A debounced change updates the stable state and logs whether B1 is pressed or released. firmware/app/app.c:42-44 performs the update and LOGI call.
node_notes.start: This step calls board_io_init before the application begins its bring-up loop. The call in firmware/app/app.c:52 prepares the platform's LED and button GPIOs.
node_notes.seed: The loop establishes its initial millisecond reference and button debounce candidate state before sampling continuously. These state variables are initialized in firmware/app/app.c:17-20.
node_notes.console_init: This step initializes the console before any application status messages are emitted. firmware/app/app.c:53 calls console_init, whose STM32 backend configures USART2 TX in firmware/platforms/stm32/console_stm32.c.
node_notes.button_changed: This condition detects a new sampled button state so the debounce candidate and its start time can be reset. The comparison is in firmware/app/app.c:33.
node_notes.startup_log: The application emits a startup message describing the LED blink and button debounce behavior. The LOGI call is in firmware/app/app.c:54 and is routed through the configured console.
node_notes.set_candidate: A changed sample becomes the new candidate and starts a fresh debounce interval. firmware/app/app.c:35-36 records both values.

sequence.title: Sequence Diagram
sequence.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Main as Core main
  participant App as Bring-up application
  participant IO as STM32 board I/O
  participant Button as PA0 user button
  participant LED as PD12 indicator LED
  participant Tick as SysTick
  participant Console as USART2 console
  participant UART as USART2 TX on PA2

  Main->>App: app_start
  App->>IO: board_io_init
  App->>Console: console_init
  App->>Console: LOGI bring-up started
  Console->>UART: Send startup log bytes

  loop Foreground loop; LED interval is 200 ms
    App->>IO: board_io_millis
    IO-->>App: Current milliseconds
    App->>IO: board_io_button_is_pressed
    IO->>Button: Sample PA0 with LL_GPIO_IsInputPinSet
    Button-->>IO: Electrical input level
    IO-->>App: Logical pressed state

    alt LED interval elapsed
      App->>IO: board_io_led_toggle
      IO->>LED: LL_GPIO_TogglePin on PD12
    else LED interval not elapsed
      Note over App: Continue button debounce processing
    end

    alt Sample differs from candidate
      App->>App: Update candidate and debounce start time
    else Sample matches candidate
      alt Candidate changed and debounce interval elapsed
        App->>App: Accept stable button state
        App->>Console: LOGI pressed or released
        Console->>UART: Send button status bytes
      else Debounce interval not complete or no stable change
        Note over App: Keep current stable button state
      end
    end

    App->>IO: board_io_wait_for_interrupt
    IO->>Tick: __WFI until interrupt
    Tick->>IO: SysTick_Handler calls board_io_stm32_systick_isr
    IO-->>App: Return after interrupt wake
  end
